proof.title: One loop from intention to proof.
proof.description: GymTrack keeps the full training relationship visible: what was planned, what was done, what changed, and what happens next.

hero.description: GymTrack exists for the work that happens after the whiteboard and before the progress photo. The sets you actually did, the meals you actually ate, the measurements that actually changed — kept in one place so coach and athlete see the same truth.

ledger.title: Training ledger — week 12
ledger.coach_body: “Tempo held well. Add 2.5 kg next week, keep rest at 90s. Nice cut on the waist — fuel stayed consistent. See you Friday.”
ledger.honest: Edits close after 24h — the log stays honest

rail.crew: Crew — the people behind the tape

origin.p1: We watched the same failure loop: athletes texting screenshots of spreadsheets, trainers juggling five group chats, and nobody quite sure what actually happened last Tuesday. Progress stalled not from lack of effort, but from lack of shared evidence.
origin.p2: So we narrowed the problem. One calendar where workouts and meals live together. One relationship that is explicit — invited, accepted, or ended. One rule that keeps everyone honest: you can correct today, not rewrite last month.
origin.card1_desc: Sets, plates, macros, or just “did it.” Speed beats perfection.
origin.card2_desc: Invite codes, not DMs. Status is visible to both sides.
origin.y2023_text: Trainer Meryem runs 22 clients across WhatsApp, Sheets, and memory. At 11pm she texts: “Did you do the 3×8?” No answer until Thursday.
origin.y2024_text: We ship a brutalist prototype: one date, two tabs — workout and meal. No followers, no feed. Just the log and a coach who can see it.
origin.y2025_text: We lock edits after a day. Complaints for a week, then trust goes up. Athletes stop backfilling a perfect month on Sunday night.
origin.y2026_text: Trainers run quiet, focused rosters. Athletes carry proof, not promises. The middle between plan and proof finally has a home.

loop.title: The loop is the product.
loop.description: Four stations, one direction. If any station is invisible, the loop breaks and coaching becomes guessing.
loop.s1_desc: Athlete records what happened — sets, meals, weight — while the memory is still warm.
loop.s2_desc: Trainer reads the ledger, not the highlight reel. Comments live on the entry itself.
loop.s3_desc: Plans are templates until assigned. Adjust load, swap movements, keep what works.
loop.s4_desc: Charts and history turn effort into evidence. Next week starts from facts.
loop.quiet_body: No likes. No streak shaming. No “you missed a day” notifications at midnight. The platform gets out of the way so the relationship can do its work.
loop.quiet_tag: — built to be boring, on purpose

principles.p1_body: If it isn’t logged, it didn’t happen. We design for the truth — even when the truth is ‘I skipped it.’ That’s still data.
principles.p2_body: A trainer with 40 clients has no clients. We cap, we surface who needs attention today, we make ending a relationship respectful.
principles.p2_meta: Invite codes · client since · today focus
principles.p3_body: Gym progress is compound interest. We optimize for ‘show up again tomorrow’ — fast logging, quiet UI, no dopamine traps.
principles.p3_meta: One tap log · no feed · calendar first

crew.title: Small team, gym hours.
crew.subtitle: We lift, we coach, we ship — in that order
crew.meryem_detail: 10y coaching, 2,000+ client weeks. Wrote the 24h rule on a gym napkin.
crew.emir_detail: Former powerlifter. Obsessed with logging speed — ‘if it takes 30s, it won’t happen.’
crew.sena_detail: Turned the ledger into a calm interface. Believes boredom is a design goal.
crew.can_detail: Keeps the log honest — clock injection, JSONB, and migrations that don’t lie.

stats_strip.reps_desc: Since Jan 2024. Not vanity — each set has weight, reps, and a date that can’t be edited after 24h.
stats_strip.avg_desc: Long enough to see a cut, a plateau, and the adjustment that breaks it.
stats_strip.ontime_desc: Logged within the day. The rest is late — and the chart shows it.

cta.description: No credit card. No onboarding maze. Log one workout, invite a coach when you’re ready — or train solo until you want eyes on the work.

metadata.title: About — GymTrack
metadata.description: Between plan and proof there is a log. GymTrack is the shared source of truth for athletes and trainers — one ledger, one relationship, one honest loop.
